Neon Auth 0.4.2-beta pins Better Auth 1.4.18 for client, cookie, and type adapters. At runtime Neon Auth imports only better-auth/client, /client/plugins, /cookies, /react and /types from that copy and forwards /api/auth requests upstream to the hosted NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL, so no 1.4.18 server handler (OAuth callback, state check, account linking, plugins) runs in-process; the app's own agent-auth server uses Better Auth 1.6.26. Neon Auth 0.5.0-beta (Better Auth 1.6.23) was published 2026-08-11; migrating to it is an auth-path change tracked in BRO-2627 and must land before this reviewBy. GHSA-q84f-53jg-9ppm (published 2026-10-27) applies only when the opt-in deviceAuthorization() plugin is enabled. The sole local Better Auth instance configures only @better-auth/agent-auth (id agent-auth), whose compiled implementation does not include deviceAuthorization; its device_authorization approval method is a separate implementation. The main entry remains a hosted Neon proxy, not a local 1.4.18 server. scripts/auth-device-advisory.test.ts evaluates the actual local configuration and guards both conditions. This is a conditional non-applicability assessment, not a claim that installed packages or the hosted provider are patched; re-review if the plugin or topology changes.

Patched Undici 7.30.1 is pinned for sandbox and jsdom, and Vercel Blob resolves patched 6.29.1. The remaining vulnerable 5.29.0 runtime branch belongs only to ConnectRPC v1 for an operator-configured Life gateway; no patched 5.x release exists. Its Busboy dependency is independently upgraded to 3.2.2 with fragmented multipart and HTTP/2 RPC integration tests. The retained advisory keys still affect Undici 5: caller-controlled proxy, cookie, WebSocket and destination configuration are not exposed, but HTTP parsing and denial-of-service residual risk remains until a ConnectRPC v2 migration. Reassessed 2026-10-27; existing deadline unchanged.
